question.worked_solution:
The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

The first term is 

$$
{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2(1)}=\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2}
$$

 

and the second term is 

$$
{a}_{2}=\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2(2)}=\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{4}.
$$

Therefore, the common ratio is 

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{4}}{\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2}}={(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2}=\frac{4}{25}.
$$

 

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{\frac{7}{10}{(-\frac{2}{5})}^{2}}{1-\frac{4}{25}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{7}{10}(\frac{4}{25})}{\frac{21}{25}} \\  & =\frac{7}{10}\cdot \frac{4}{25}\cdot \frac{25}{21} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
